parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use a correct double-angle formula to expand $\sin4x$ - *M1, e.g. $2\sin2x\cos2x$.

Use a correct double-angle formula to obtain an expression in $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ - dM1, e.g. $4\sin x\cos x(2\cos^2x-1)$.

Obtain the stated identity from fully correct working - A1, AG.

Alternative method 1: rearrange the RHS with a correct double-angle formula, e.g. $2\sin2x(2\cos^2x-1)$ - *M1; obtain an expression in $\sin2x$ and $\cos2x$, e.g. $2\sin2x\cos2x$ - dM1; obtain the identity - A1, AG.

Alternative method 2: use the angle-sum formula to expand $\sin4x$ as far as an expression in $\sin x,\cos x,\sin2x,\cos2x$, e.g. $\sin x(\cos x\cos2x-\sin x\sin2x)+\cos x(\sin x\cos2x+\cos x\sin2x)$ - *M1. Use a correct double-angle formula to obtain an expression in $\sin x,\cos x$, e.g. $\sin x\cos x(2\cos^2x-1)-2\sin^3x\cos x+\sin x\cos x(2\cos^2x-1)+2\sin x\cos^3x$ - dM1. Obtain the identity - A1.

Printed total: 3.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use the identity to obtain $p\int\sin x\cos^6x\,dx+q\int\sin x\cos^4x\,dx$ - B1; specifically $8\int\sin x\cos^6x\,dx-4\int\sin x\cos^4x\,dx$. Accept correct-form terms without integral signs or $dx$.

Obtain $r\cos^7x+s\cos^5x$ - B1.

Obtain $-\dfrac87\cos^7x+\dfrac45\cos^5x$ - B1. If using $u=\cos x$, accept $-\dfrac87u^7+\dfrac45u^5$.

Use the correct limits in $r\cos^7x+s\cos^5x$ - M1; must be evaluated, e.g. $-\dfrac87\dfrac1{8\sqrt2}+\dfrac45\dfrac1{4\sqrt2}+\dfrac87-\dfrac45$.

Obtain $\dfrac1{35}(\sqrt2+12)$ - A1, or exact simplified equivalent (e.g. two terms).

Printed total: 5.
